question.value: Identify (sub)stellar companions down to ~20 au separation in the Lupus Molecular Cloud and investigate the effects of stellar multiplicity on circumstellar disc properties (masses, sizes, brightness profiles).

claims.hypothesis: Visual stellar companions (separations 20-4800 au) significantly alter the overall protoplanetary disc mass and size distributions.
claims.experiment: Combine VLT/NACO AO multiplicity survey of 105 Lupus YSOs (and 236 Ophiuchus YSOs) with ALMA continuum disc masses and sizes using Kaplan-Meier survival analysis and KS tests.
claims.result: KS test comparing single vs multiple disc mass distributions up to 50 M_earth yields p-values of 40% (Lupus) and 51% (Lupus+Ophiuchus), while discs with M_dust > 50 M_earth and R_dust > 70-80 au only occur around single stars.
claims.finding: Visual companions with separations > 20 au mostly affect discs in the upper 10% of the mass and size distributions; for the remaining 80-90% of discs, single and multiple distributions are nearly identical.

evidence.quote: stellar companions with separations $>$ 20 au mostly affect discs in the upper 10$\%$ of the disc mass and size distributions.

A Kolmogorov-Smirnov test comparing the distributions of singles versus multiples gives a p-value of 40% for Lupus and 51% for Lupus and Ophiuchus combined. These high p-values suggest that the distributions are nearly identical.

claims.hypothesis: Primary stars in multiple systems host more massive circumstellar discs than secondary companions.
claims.experiment: Compare Kaplan-Meier cumulative dust mass distributions of primary components versus companion components in Lupus and in the combined Lupus+Ophiuchus sample.
claims.result: In all 4 Lupus systems with both components detected by ALMA and across the combined Lupus+Ophiuchus sample, primary disc dust masses are systematically higher than secondary disc masses.
claims.finding: Discs around primary stars are systematically more massive than those around secondary stars, consistent with stellar mass dependence and smaller tidal truncation radii / shorter lifetimes for secondaries.

evidence.quote: Discs around the primary stars are indeed systematically more massive than the ones around the secondary stars.
Discs around primary stars are systematically more massive than the ones around their companions.

claims.hypothesis: Discs in multiple systems have more compact radial surface density / brightness profiles than discs around single stars.
claims.experiment: Extract and compare 147 deprojected normalized 1.3 mm ALMA continuum radial brightness profiles (using imfit inclination and PA for sources with peak SNR > 10) for single and multiple systems in Lupus and Ophiuchus.
claims.result: Single stars span a wider range of masses for a given disc size and multiple-system discs exhibit systematically more compact normalized 1.3 mm radial brightness profiles.
claims.finding: Discs in multiple systems are clearly more compact than single-star discs, suggesting differences in their surface density profiles.

evidence.quote: The figure includes 147 radial profiles between single and binary stars for both samples. Discs in multiple systems are clearly more compact than single star discs.

Discs around stars in multiple systems have flux distributions that tend to be much more compact than those seen for single stars. This suggests significant differences in their surface density profiles.

why_this_data.value: Lupus Class II and Class III YSOs already had complete ALMA millimetre continuum coverage constraining disc masses and sizes; VLT/NACO L' star-hopping AO observations provided a fast way to complete the visual multiplicity census down to ~20 au and combine with the identical NIR-ODISEA Ophiuchus survey.

evidence.quote: All 105 targets have millimetre ALMA data available, which provide constraints on disc masses and sizes.
In short, we used very quick (0.16–0.17 s) $L^{\prime}$ band filter exposures with the “star-hopping” technique to minimize overheads and maximize the number of observed objects.

why_this_method.value: Kaplan-Meier estimator via lifelines accounts for ALMA continuum non-detections (censored data); deprojected 1.3 mm brightness profiles serve as a proxy for radial mass distribution without requiring full radiative transfer modeling.

evidence.quote: we show cumulative distribution functions of disc mass, accounting for non-detections using the python package lifelines (cite: 2019JOSS....4.1317D), a Kaplan-Meier (KM) product estimator

Deriving accurate surface density profiles requires radiative transfer modeling, which is outside the scope of this paper. However, at 1.3 mm the brightness profile is well correlated with the distribution of mass as a function of radius.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Radiative transfer modeling to derive accurate surface density profiles was considered outside the scope of the paper, using 1.3 mm brightness profiles instead.

evidence.quote: Deriving accurate surface density profiles requires radiative transfer modeling, which is outside the scope of this paper. However, at 1.3 mm the brightness profile is well correlated with the distribution of mass as a function of radius.

limitations_admitted.value: Binaries with projected separations < 20 au (0.1 arcsec AO diffraction limit in L' band at 150 pc) and spectroscopic binaries are not resolved, and companions wider than ~4800 au fall outside the NACO field of view.

evidence.quote: The minimum separation probed by our observations is related to the AO diffraction limit of the instrument in $L^{\prime}$ band. This is 0.1$''$, i.e. $\sim$18 au at 150 pc. Binaries with separations closer than 20 au would not be resolved in this study.
Our study is sensitive to visual binaries with projected separations between 20–4800 au —spectroscopic, tight, and large separation binaries are not included in our statistics.

limitations_admitted.value: The 12 M_Jup planetary-mass companion candidate around 2MASS J16095628-3859518 has a 16.4% (~17%) background probability and requires a second epoch to confirm common proper motion.

evidence.quote: We estimate the probability of this object being a background star to be $\sim$17%, hence a second-epoch observation is needed to rule out this possibility.

referee_caveats_inferred: Exclusion of the 20 faintest (late-M) YSOs from NACO observations could bias the overall multiplicity fraction and the lower tail of the disc mass distribution.
Unconfirmed boundness for several wide/faint companions lacking Gaia DR2 parallaxes for the secondary relies only on statistical TRILEGAL background probabilities.
Combining Class II (Band 6, 0.25 arcsec) and Class III (Band 7, 0.7 arcsec) ALMA surveys mixes different wavelengths and angular resolutions.

reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: ~10-50 GB (published ALMA continuum images/tables for ~125 targets plus VLT/NACO NIR frames)
reproducibility.score_reason: ALMA disc masses and sizes are directly taken from published tables in Ansdell et al. (2018) and Lovell et al. (2020), and all ESO/ALMA program IDs and detected binaries are tabulated, though the full 105-object master table and radial profile extraction parameters are not explicitly provided.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: All ALMA and VLT/NACO datasets are public, the published catalog tables in Ansdell et al. (2018) and Lovell et al. (2020) provide the exact disc masses and sizes, and the statistical comparison (Kaplan-Meier curves and KS tests) produces clear numeric benchmarks.
